newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares close mixed in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares close mixed in dull trade.

text.p: Indian shares ended mixed in dull trade across major bourses on Monday in the absence of investor interest amid hopes the government might initiate steps to revive markets, brokers said.
Brokers said the market mood remained subdued as foreign institutional investors preferred to maintain a low profile, limiting their year-end commitments.
"No one wants to keep his positions long at this time of the year, especially in speculative shares," said a broker.
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index fell 11.14 points to 2,815.06.

Brokers said the markets were keenly awaiting a meeting the market watchdog Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has called in New Delhi on Tuesday to discuss measures to help boost investor confidence.

Delhi shares closed marginally higher in mixed trade amid expectations that SEBI might introduce steps to boost investor confidenece. The Delhi Stock Exchange sensitive index closed 1.22 points higher at 637.01.
But some brokers are sceptical about the outcome.
"Not much is expected of the SEBI meeting," said a broker. "There could be some relaxation in procedures."
The Madras index fell marginally by 7.26 points to 2,913.87 while the Calcutta index rose 0.44 points to 395.91.
Brokers said foreign institutioanl investors (FIIs) were generally absent in the major bourses because of their low year-end commitments and approaching Christmas holidays.
Stock broker Sunil Kothari said domestic financial institutions had been inactive in the market for want of funds.
"Blue chip prices have down drastically. It's time to buy. But who has got money to buy, except FIIs," Kothari said. "And I don't think FIIs will come into the picture before January.
